4 Transport protocols for R1 Services
The R1 interface is defined between the rApps and the Non-RT RIC framework, as defined in R1GAP [11].
The layers of the protocol stack for the R1 interface are described in the following chapters:

• TCP [2] provides the communica?on service at the transport layer,
  • TLS [10] is used as specified in SPS [13], clause 4.2 to provide secure HTTP [17] [18] connec?ons,
  • HTTP [16] [17] [18] is used as applica?on-level protocol,
  • The data interchange layer cons?tutes the transport of documents in the JSON format [8].

As network layer at least one of IPv6 [9] or IPv4 [1] shall be supported.
TCP [2] shall be supported as transport protocol.
NOTE: When using TCP as the transport protocol, an HTTP connec?on is mapped to a TCP connec?on.
The specifica?on of security controls on the R1 interface in SRS [12], clause 5.2.6.2 shall be followed.

These security controls refer to the detailed specifica?on of the support and use of TLS v1.2 and TLS v1.3 (IETF RFC 8446 [10]), and OAuth2.0 [14] with JSON Web Tokens (JWT) (IETF RFC 7519 [15]) in the O-RAN TS SPS [13] .
As applica?on layer, HTTP/1.1 [17] shall be supported, and HTTP/2 [18] should be supported. The HTTP seman?cs as defined in IETF RFC 9110 [16] shall be supported.
HTTP over TLS (as defined in IETF RFC 9112 for HTTP/1.1 [17] and in IETF RFC 9113 [18] for HTTP/2) shall be supported.
HTTP details such as use of standard headers, custom headers, error codes, methods, URIs etc. will be specified in Applica?on Protocols for R1 Services.
The default TCP port numbers should be used for HTTP opera?on.
As a data interchange format, JSON [8] shall be supported.
The Kaja based protocol stack for the R1 interface includes the following layers:

• TCP [2] provides the communica?on service at the transport layer,
  • TLS [10] is used to provide secure connec?ons at the security layer,
  • The Kaja Protocol Guide [20] is used at the applica?on layer,
  • The data interchange layer cons?tutes the serializa?on format in which data are represented.
